sources.name: NOAA GML Trends in Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide (Mauna Loa and global marine surface)
sources.publisher: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory (Boulder, CO); the Mauna Loa record before May 1974 comes from Scripps Institution of Oceanography
sources.measures: CO2 dry-air mole fraction in ppm (micromol/mol). Mauna Loa: daily, weekly, monthly (raw and deseasonalized) and annual means. Global marine boundary layer: monthly and annual means. Annual growth rate in ppm/yr. Every value comes with an uncertainty.
sources.coverage: Mauna Loa (19.5N, 155.6W) from March 1958 to August 2026 (monthly). Global marine surface mean from 1979 to June 2026 (monthly), with annual values to 2025. One point site plus a global average; no gridded data.
sources.latest_release: Version 2026-09. Files created Sat 5 Sep 2026. Latest Mauna Loa month is Aug 2026 at 427.55 ppm (Aug 2025: 425.48). Latest global month is Jun 2026 at 427.62 ppm. Annual 2025: Mauna Loa 427.35 +/- 0.12 ppm, global 425.62 +/- 0.05 ppm.
sources.update_cadence: Monthly, around the 5th. Mauna Loa daily and weekly files update more often. The most recent year can be revised after recalibration.
sources.format: CSV (and TXT), with comment lines starting with '#' for metadata, citation and creation timestamp
sources.license: Work of the US federal government, so public domain in the US (17 U.S.C. 105). File header: 'These data are made freely available to the public and the scientific community in the belief that their wide dissemination will lead to greater understanding and new scientific insights.' NOAA asks users to 'include relevant citation text in publications' and suggests co-authorship when the data are central to a publication. There are no NC or ND terms and no registration.
sources.citation: Global: Lan, X., Tans, P. and K.W. Thoning: Trends in globally-averaged CO2 determined from NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory measurements. Version 2026-09, https://doi.org/10.15138/9N0H-ZH07. Mauna Loa (credit line from data.html): Dr. Xin Lan, NOAA/GML (gml.noaa.gov/ccgg/trends/) and Dr. Ralph Keeling, Scripps Institution of Oceanography (scrippsco2.ucsd.edu/). Global-mean method reference in the file header: Conway et al., 1994, JGR 99(D11).
sources.status: ACTIVE BUT AT RISK. (1) The President's FY2026 budget proposed terminating NOAA OAR climate labs, including GML and Mauna Loa Observatory (MLO): Mongabay Jul 2025, Hawaii Public Radio 13 Aug 2025, EHN. (2) The lease on the Hilo support office (where 8 staff remotely operate MLO; $164,391/yr) was due to expire 31 Aug 2025. Hawaii's delegation introduced a support resolution on 28 Aug 2025 (Big Island Now 29 Aug 2025; Aloha State Daily). (3) Congress rejected eliminating OAR for FY2026. This comes from an Inside Climate News article of 29 Apr 2026, which I fetched. The detail of a January 2026 law funding NOAA at about $6B with a no-close directive is only in a search snippet of Forbes (30 May 2026); the full article returned HTTP 403. (4) In April 2026 a pause in grant funding caused GML staff furloughs; funds were released 16 Apr 2026 (ICN). (5) The FY2027 request again proposes eliminating OAR and a 26% NOAA cut that would defund MLO (ICN 29 Apr 2026). (6) Per gml.noaa.gov/obop/mlo, the temporary MLO access road was completed 26 Mar 2026, but it is 'still unclear when utility infrastructure will be replaced and power re-established'. Data are still flowing: the Aug 2026 value was published 5 Sep 2026.

The weekly, daily, gr_gl and trend_gl files are listed on the data pages but I did not fetch each one.
sources.site_use: Core 'now' number and hero chart: the Keeling Curve from monthly co2_mm_mlo, raw plus deseasonalized, with a toggle to the global marine mean. Annual growth-rate bars from co2_gr_mlo/co2_gr_gl show acceleration and El Nino years. Global annual means feed the '% above pre-industrial' calculation (with the IGCC 1750 baseline). Ingest at build time into a versioned snapshot that stores the file creation timestamp and version string (2026-09) next to every number.
sources.caveats: Mauna Loa and the global marine mean are different numbers (2025: 427.35 vs 425.62). Always label which one is shown. Values from Dec 2022 to 4 Jul 2023 are from Maunakea. WMO GAW global means differ slightly (2024: 423.9 WMO vs 422.79 NOAA) because station selection differs.

sources.license: US federal public domain. There is no separate licence text; GML data-use language applies.

The method switched to effective radiative forcing in 2023, which shifts values slightly for all years. Last year shown is 2024.

sources.coverage: Mauna Loa from March 1958 to Aug 2026 (in situ monthly). Flask delta-13C from 1977/1980 to Dec 2024. Other stations (South Pole, La Jolla and others) are on the same site.
sources.latest_release: monthly_in_situ_co2_mlo.csv: 'Baseline data through 19-Sep-2026 from archive dated 21-Sep-2026'; Aug 2026 427.31 ppm. Flask delta-13C file: 'archive dated 06-Jun-2025', last value Dec 2024 -8.71 per mil.
sources.update_cadence: In situ updated monthly or more often; flask isotopes lag by about 1 year
sources.format: CSV with a quoted text header block; missing values are -99.99 or NaN
sources.license: CC BY 4.0. Station page: 'Scripps CO2 program data and graphics on scrippsco2.ucsd.edu are licensed under a CC BY license, Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License'. Attribution goes to Scripps Institution of Oceanography at UC San Diego. The site also notes that co-authorship may sometimes be appropriate.

sources.name: Antarctic Ice Cores Revised 800KYr CO2 composite (Bereiter et al. 2015)
sources.publisher: Univ. of Bern / EPICA consortium; archived by NOAA NCEI World Data Service for Paleoclimatology
sources.measures: Atmospheric CO2 in ppm with 1-sigma uncertainty, against gas age in years before 1950 (yr BP)
sources.coverage: From -51 yr BP (2001 AD) back to 805,669 yr BP. Composite of Law Dome, Dome C, WAIS, Siple Dome, TALDICE, EDML and Vostok.
sources.latest_release: Contributed 4 Feb 2015 (final dataset). The maximum before the industrial era (age > 1000 yr BP) is 298.60 ppm at 335,102 yr BP. The minimum is about 172 to 175 ppm (MIS 16).
sources.format: Fixed-width/TSV text with a NOAA paleo template header
sources.license: Distributed by NOAA NCEI (US government). Header: 'Please cite Publication, and Online_Resource and date accessed when using these data.' No restrictive terms.
sources.citation: Bereiter, B., Eggleston, S., Schmitt, J., Nehrbass-Ahles, C., Stocker, T.F., Fischer, H., Kipfstuhl, S. and Chappellaz, J. (2015): Revision of the EPICA Dome C CO2 record from 800 to 600 kyr before present. Geophysical Research Letters, doi:10.1002/2014GL061957. Online resource: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/paleo-search/study/17975 (accessed <date>).
sources.status: Archived and final. Low risk, but NCEI is a NOAA office, so keep a local snapshot.
sources.url_check: The study landing page returned an empty JS shell to WebFetch. The data file (curl) has header lines 'Antarctic Ice Cores Revised 800KYr CO2 Data', Contribution_Date 2015-02-04, the composite segment list and DOI 10.1002/2014GL061957. An awk scan over all rows with age > 1000 yr BP returned 'max 298.60 age 335102.31'. First row -51.03, 368.02; last row 805668.87, 207.29.
sources.site_use: The '800,000 years' zoom-out chart: glacial cycles stay between about 175 and 300 ppm, then today's 427 ppm spike, with NOAA's latest value appended and clearly marked as a different source. Headline 'highest in 800,000 years'.
sources.caveats: Age is years before 1950, so convert with AD = 1950 - age. The most recent part is Law Dome (to 2001), so don't double-plot with Law Dome. Ice-core air is smoothed over decades to centuries, so it cannot rule out brief spikes; say this in the explainer. The 800k claim is about the ice-core record only.

headline_numbers.statement: In 2025 the air held 425.6 ppm of CO2 on global average (427.4 ppm at Mauna Loa), the highest ever measured.

drilldown_paths: THE KEELING CURVE, ZOOM OUT: Mauna Loa daily, weekly and monthly (NOAA co2_daily/weekly/mm_mlo; Scripps monthly_in_situ as twin) -> seasonal 'breathing' explainer (raw vs deseasonalized columns) -> annual growth-rate bars with El Nino years (co2_gr_mlo / co2_gr_gl) -> 2000 years (Law Dome law2018splines CO2spl) -> 800,000 years (Bereiter antarctica2015co2composite) with today's dot appended (co2_annmean_gl 2025). Ends on the 'highest in 800,000 years' headline.

HOW DO WE KNOW IT'S US? Rising CO2 (NOAA) -> isotopic fingerprint: delta-13C falling from -7.60 to -8.71 per mil (Scripps monthly_flask_c13_mlo; Law Dome law2018d13c-co2) = fossil/plant carbon -> 'with and without humans' simulation vs observations (IPCC SPM.1 panel_b gmst_changes_model_and_obs.csv) -> attribution waterfall GHG +1.63 / aerosols and other -0.26 / natural +0.04 = 1.37 deg C (IGCC Assessment-Update-2025_GMST_headlines.csv).

WHICH GASES, HOW MUCH HEAT? Forcing stack 1750-2025 by agent (IGCC ERF_best_aggregates.csv: CO2, CH4, N2O, halogens, ozone, aerosols, land use, solar, volcanic) -> click a gas -> its concentration curve (NOAA co2/ch4/n2o/sf6 annmean_gl + Law Dome pre-1958) -> its growth rate -> link to the emissions-sector domain (where it comes from) -> NOAA AGGI table (AGGI_Table.csv) showing CFCs falling after the Montreal Protocol, as proof that policy works.

HOW HOT IS IT, AND ARE THE THERMOMETERS AGREEING? Today's global temperature and daily anomaly spaghetti by year (Climate Pulse era5_daily_series_2t_global.csv; SST 60S-60N) -> annual multi-dataset chart re-baselined to 1850-1900 with every offset shown: HadCRUT5.2 (with 95% CI), NOAAGlobalTemp v6.1, GISTEMP v4, ERA5 +0.88, optionally Berkeley Earth labelled NC -> WMO consensus 1.44 +/- 0.13 (Zenodo dashboard; method code climate-indicator-manager) -> 2000-year context (IPCC SPM1_1-2000_recon.csv) -> human-induced vs observed (IGCC).

WHERE I LIVE: World map of the latest month's anomaly -> country (OWID monthly-temperature-anomalies, from ERA5, vs that country's 1991-2020 mean) -> the country's monthly history since 1940 and its warming stripes -> latitude-band context: Arctic warms fastest (NOAAGlobalTemp aravg.*.60N.90N vs 90S.90N; HadCRUT NH/SH summary series) -> back to the global causes.

THE BUDGET CLOCK (WHAT YOU CAN DO): Human-induced warming 1.37 deg C rising 0.27 deg C/decade (IGCC headlines and rates) -> remaining CO2 budget for 1.5 / 1.7 / 2.0 deg C at 50% (IGCC carbon_budget CSVs: 130 GtCO2 for 1.5 deg C from 2026; 1.7 and 2.0 deg C budgets from the same file family) -> years left at the current 42 GtCO2/yr -> per-person framing and a hand-off to the emissions/actions domain -> methane as the fast lever (short lifetime about 9 yr per the WMO GHG Bulletin; CH4 ERF 0.57 W/m2) -> aerosol cleanup unmasks warming (aerosol ERF -0.96 W/m2), so cutting CO2 is still essential.

WHO MEASURES THIS, AND IS IT SAFE? Provenance panel on every chart (file URL, version, file-creation timestamp, DOI, transformation) -> 'the observatories' page: Mauna Loa (NOAA GML) status timeline (2022 lava, Maunakea substitution, March 2026 road, FY2026/FY2027 budget fights) -> how the WMO GAW and NOAA global numbers differ (423.9 vs 422.79 ppm for 2024) -> what citizens can do to defend public climate monitoring.
research.action_links:
INDIVIDUALS. (1) The carbon budget makes the stakes personal. About 130 GtCO2 is left for a 50% chance of 1.5 deg C, roughly 3 years of current emissions (IGCC 2025, Forster et al. 2026, doi:10.5194/essd-18-3889-2026; indicators.climate.copernicus.eu). Cutting CO2 is the dominant lever because CO2 is about 2.37 of the 3.10 W/m2 of human forcing (IGCC ERF_best_aggregates.csv), and the WMO GHG Bulletin No. 21 says net-zero CO2 'must be the focus of climate action'. Link the visitor from here to the emissions and actions domains (household energy, transport, diet), with those domains' own sources. (2) Methane is the fast lever. It lasts about 9 years in the air versus millennia of CO2 effects (WMO GHG Bulletin No. 21, p.2), and it is now 2.65x pre-industrial (NOAA GML). Food waste, diet and leaky gas appliances connect to it via the emissions domain. (3) Refrigerants: the AGGI page documents CFC declines under the Montreal Protocol and the HFC phase-down that began in 2019 (gml.noaa.gov/aggi/aggi.html). Proper disposal of fridges and air-conditioning units and choosing low-GWP appliances are concrete, evidence-backed actions.

COMMUNITIES AND ACTIVISTS. (4) Every number on the site carries a file URL, version and DOI, so activists can cite it in testimony or letters (NOAA GML version 2026-09 DOIs; HadCRUT5 OGL acknowledgement; IGCC CC BY data). (5) Defend the measurements themselves. NOAA's FY2026 and FY2027 budget requests proposed eliminating OAR, including the Global Monitoring Laboratory and Mauna Loa (Inside Climate News, 29 Apr 2026; Hawaii Public Radio, 13 Aug 2025). Congress rejected the FY2026 cut, and an April 2026 grant pause furloughed GML staff (ICN). The site can explain the appropriations timeline and encourage contacting representatives, while staying non-partisan and evidence-led.

POLICYMAKERS. (6) The WMO State of the Global Climate 2025 (1.44 +/- 0.13 deg C; 2015-2025 the 11 warmest years) and IGCC 2025 (human-induced 1.37 deg C, 0.27 deg C/decade) are the annual evidence inputs to the UNFCCC process. Cite the CC BY dashboard (doi:10.5281/zenodo.19737593) and the IGCC data (doi:10.5281/zenodo.21494229). (7) The Montreal Protocol case (AGGI CFC series) shows that binding international agreements measurably change atmospheric composition. (8) Aerosol cleanup unmasks warming (aerosol ERF about -0.96 W/m2, IGCC), so air-quality policy must be paired with GHG cuts.
research.gaps_and_risks:
1. US FEDERAL RISK (highest). NOAA GML (the CO2/CH4/N2O/SF6 trends and the AGGI) and Mauna Loa were proposed for elimination in both FY2026 and FY2027. FY2026 was rejected by Congress, and the FY2027 request seeks a 26% NOAA cut and OAR elimination again (Inside Climate News, 29 Apr 2026). GML staff were furloughed during the April 2026 grant pause. The Hilo office lease was a flashpoint in Aug 2025. MLO power has still not been restored, though the temporary road reopened 26 Mar 2026. The 2025 AGGI has not been published (the page still says 'Updated Fall 2025' with 2024 data), which may signal delay. NASA GISS lost its building (31 May 2025), and GISTEMP depends on NOAA GHCN/ERSST. Mitigations:
- snapshot every source file at ingest (raw bytes plus SHA-256 plus fetch timestamp) into our own storage (R2 or similar fits the <$20/mo budget);
- record a Wayback Machine URL for each file;
- add non-US fallbacks: WMO GAW/WDCGG for GHGs, and HadCRUT5/ERA5 for temperature.

2. LICENSING. Berkeley Earth is CC BY-NC 4.0, and its public files are stale: global ends Dec 2024, country files end May 2016. Do not use it for country drill-downs or bundle it in open CSV downloads without NC labelling. WMO report text is WMO-copyright; use the CC BY dashboard data instead. The WMO GHG Bulletin/WDCGG redistribution terms are unclear, so cite only. HadCRUT5 OGL requires an exact acknowledgement line with version and download date in every CSV. Copernicus needs 'Contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information 2026'. The CDS API needs a free ECMWF account (key in macOS Keychain); Climate Pulse CSVs do not.

3. BASELINE AND DEFINITION TRAPS. Each dataset uses a different baseline:

| Dataset | Native baseline |
|---|---|
| GISTEMP | 1951-1980 |
| HadCRUT | 1961-1990 |
| NOAAGlobalTemp v6.1 asc | 1991-2020 |
| NOAA Climate at a Glance CSV | 1901-2000 |
| ERA5 | 1991-2020 (+0.88 offset) |
| Berkeley Earth | 1951-1980 |
| OWID temperature | 1861-1890 |
| IGCC / WMO | 1850-1900 |

Every transformation must be stored and shown. Partial-year rows appear in the annual files (HadCRUT 2026, NOAA 2026, OWID 2026) and must be excluded or flagged. There are several legitimate 'global CO2' numbers (NOAA marine-surface 425.62, Mauna Loa 427.35, IGCC 425.65, WMO GAW 423.9 for 2024), so label the station or network on every number. The 1750 baselines differ between Law Dome splines (277.0 ppm / 706.9 ppb) and AR6/IGCC (278.4 / 729.2); pick IGCC/AR6 site-wide. CO2 growth can be the difference of annual means (3.33/3.44) or Jan-to-Jan (3.72 ppm for 2024).

4. REVISIONS. NOAA marks the latest year provisional; CH4 annual increases change 'significantly'. ERA5 daily values are PRELIMINARY for 2-5 days. HadCRUT, NOAA and IGCC change versions (HadCRUT 5.1 to 5.2 in Sep 2026; NOAA v6.0 to v6.1 in Mar 2026; IGCC tags on GitHub, so pin to IGCC-2025a rather than main). Store version strings and never silently overwrite. Show 'as of <file timestamp>' on every card.

5. INTERPRETATION RISK. IGCC carbon-budget CSVs encode assumptions in their file names. The headline 130 GtCO2 is a rounded value from the hdT_1.24 file at 50%; another variant gives 97.6, and FaIR-included gives 188. Cite the paper value and document the exact file and cell, or activists may get contradictory numbers.

6. COVERAGE GAPS NOT SOLVED HERE.
- Satellite column CO2/CH4 (OCO-2/3, Copernicus CAMS) is not assessed.
- AGAGE (an independent CH4/N2O/halocarbon network; requires accepting a data policy, last bulk release Dec 2024) is not included.
- Country-level temperature relies on OWID's processing of ERA5; the long-term fix is to compute country means ourselves from ERA5 monthly at build time.
- Ocean heat content, sea level, ice and extremes belong to the 'consequences' domains, though IGCC also ships sea-level and marine-heatwave CSVs.

7. FRAGILE URLS. Several Scripps deep links now 404 after the site move (current files are on keelinglabsites.ucsd.edu). NOAAGlobalTemp file names embed yyyymm. Climate Pulse has no monthly CSV at the guessed paths. Some landing pages (NCEI paleo study, CSIRO DAP, Climate Pulse) are JS-only and could not be read by fetch, so link them for humans but ingest from the verified direct-file URLs.

Both co2_gr_mlo.csv and co2_gr_gl.csv have the header line 'Annual CO2 mole fraction increase (ppm) from Jan 1 through Dec 31.' - GitHub repo: GPL-3.0, pushed 2026-09-30.
- WMO copyright text: 'Short extracts ... may be reproduced without authorization, provided that the complete source is clearly indicated'.

CORRECTIONS:
(1) Headline value. The WMO one-pager PDF (wmo.int/sites/default/files/2026-03/State of the Climate 2025_1 pager_final.pdf) says '1.43 +/- 0.13 C above the 1850-1900 average', not 1.44.
(2) Dataset count. The dashboard (global_mean_temperature.html and tas_summary.csv, last_revised 2026-03-17) uses NINE datasets: Berkeley Earth Hires, CMA-GMST, CMST v3, DCENT-I, ERA5, GISTEMP, HadCRUT5 (5.1.0.0), JRA-3Q, NOAAGlobalTemp v6.0. Their 2025 mean is 1.434. Two rank 2025 second (DCENT-I 1.4389 and GISTEMP 1.4536); seven rank it third. The '8 datasets / 1.44' figure appears to come from an earlier press release.
(3) Zenodo has no 'v2' version string. The record is the 2025 dashboard; the 2024 dashboard (zenodo 15205854) is the previous version in the same concept.
(4) Method. Each dataset is rebaselined to 1981-2010 and then 0.69 C is added. The research's own plan (each dataset minus its own 1850-1900 or 1880-1900 mean) is a different method, so it cannot claim to copy WMO.
(5) tas_summary.csv has the BADC rights field 'TBD'. It embeds Berkeley Earth (BY-NC) and HadCRUT (OGL) derived columns, so the record-level CC BY does not clear upstream terms. Redistribute only the consolidated or open columns.
(6) WMO-No. 1391 is only partly verified: ISBN 978-92-63-11391-7 appears on the 'Significant Weather and Climate Events 2025' supplement PDF. The main-report number could not be read from the JS-only library page.

verification.headline_number_checks:
1. CO2 2025: CONFIRMED.
- Global 425.62 +/-0.05 (co2_annmean_gl.csv, created Sat Sep 5 03:55:32 2026).
- Mauna Loa 427.35 +/-0.12 (co2_annmean_mlo.csv).
- Latest month Aug 2026 427.55 (co2_mm_mlo.csv); the landing page shows the same, 'Last updated: Sep 05, 2026'.

2. +52.9% above 1750: CONFIRMED. 425.62 / 278.377857 = 1.5289. The IGCC-2025a ghg_concentrations.csv row 1750.5 is verified at the pinned tag. The Law Dome 1750 spline is 277.01, which gives +53.6%. The WMO GHG Bulletin No. 21 says 152% (for 2024).

3. +127 ppm above the 800k maximum: CONFIRMED. An independent awk scan gives a maximum of 298.60 at 335,102.31 yr BP (age > 1000) and a minimum of 173.71 at 667,409.86 yr BP. 425.62 - 298.60 = 127.02.

4. '3.33 ppm at Mauna Loa in 2024, largest in 67-yr record': VALUE CONFIRMED, DERIVATION WRONG, FRAMING WEAK.
- co2_gr_mlo.csv: 2024 3.33, 2023 3.32, 2016 3.03, 2025 2.23 (all +/-0.11).
- The file header defines the value as 'Annual CO2 mole fraction increase (ppm) from Jan 1 through Dec 31', not a difference of annual means. The difference of annual means would be 3.53 at MLO and 3.44 globally.
- 3.33 vs 3.32 is a statistical tie.
- A stronger, verified headline: global increase 3.76 +/-0.11 ppm in 2024 (co2_gr_gl.csv), versus the previous maximum of 2.95 in 2015. The 2025 global increase was 2.06 +/-0.08.

5. Methane x2.65: CONFIRMED. 1935.94 / 729.2 = 2.655. ch4_annmean_gl 2025 = 1935.94 +/-0.48; IGCC 1750.5 CH4 = 729.2. WMO gives 266% for 2024.

6. Temperature 2024/2025: MOSTLY CONFIRMED, WMO VALUE CORRECTED.
- HadCRUT.5.2.0.0: 1.187449 and 1.0732167, minus a 1850-1900 mean of -0.359436, giving 1.547 and 1.433.
- ERA5: daily means 0.719 and 0.592. The C3S GCH2025 PDF gives +0.72 / +0.59 vs 1991-2020, i.e. 1.60 and 1.47 vs pre-industrial.
- GISTEMP: J-D 1.29 and 1.19, minus a 1880-1900 mean of -0.2238, giving 1.51 and 1.41.
- NOAAGlobalTemp v6.1: 0.646727 and 0.514181, minus a 1850-1900 mean of -0.776881, giving 1.42 and 1.29.
- WMO: CORRECTED to 1.43 +/-0.13 C (final State of the Global Climate 2025 one-pager), using NINE datasets. The dashboard tas_summary 2025 mean is 1.434. Under the WMO method (rebaseline to 1981-2010, then +0.69 C), 2025 is HadCRUT5 (5.1) 1.3945, GISTEMP 1.4536, NOAA v6.0 1.4158, ERA5 1.4746.
